theory.intro: A **wage** pays per hour, a **salary** is a fixed yearly amount split into equal pays, **piecework** pays per task, and **commission** and **royalties** pay a percentage of sales. Penalty rates for overtime and weekend work, allowances, bonuses and leave loading are extra.
facts: $\text{Total pay} = \text{pay per period} \times \text{number of periods}$, so $\text{pay per period} = \dfrac{\text{total pay}}{\text{number of periods}}$ and $\text{number of periods} = \dfrac{\text{total pay}}{\text{pay per period}}$.
Four weeks is **not** a month, so change between weekly and monthly pay through the yearly amount, never by $4$.
Penalty rates multiply the normal hourly rate: time and a half is $\times 1.5$, double time is $\times 2$, double time and a half is $\times 2.5$.
$\text{Overtime pay} = \text{normal rate} \times \text{overtime hours} \times \text{penalty rate}$, and $\text{total pay} = \text{normal pay} + \text{overtime pay}$.
**Equivalent normal hours**: add $1.5 \times$ the time-and-a-half hours and $2 \times$ the double-time hours to the ordinary hours, then multiply by the normal rate.
On a **sliding scale** the rate changes past a set number of tasks, so work out each band separately and add the results.

Commission and royalties are a percentage of sales: $\text{commission} = \text{percentage} \times \text{sales}$, and with a **retainer**, $\text{total pay} = \text{retainer} + \text{percentage} \times \text{sales}$.
Leave loading is an extra $17.5\%$ of $4$ weeks' pay, so $\text{holiday pay} = 4 \times \text{weekly pay} \times 1.175$.
steps: Identify the type of earning and write the matching formula
Add any extra payments, such as overtime, allowances, bonuses or leave loading

foundation.question_text:
A barista at a café is paid $\$24.60$ per hour and works $32$ hours in a week.
Find her weekly pay.

A hairdresser is paid $\$28.40$ per hour and works $6$ hours a day, $5$ days a week.
Find her fortnightly pay.

A supermarket shelf stacker earned $\$643.95$ for $27$ hours of work.
Find his hourly rate of pay.

A delivery driver is paid $\$21.60$ per hour and earned $\$842.40$ last week.
Find the number of hours he worked.

An apprentice electrician's normal rate of pay is $\$19.80$ per hour.
Find the rate he is paid at double time and a half.

A kitchen hand is paid $\$22.40$ per hour.
In one week he works $34$ ordinary hours and $5$ hours of overtime at time and a half.
Find his total pay for the week.

A warehouse supervisor is paid a salary of $\$78\,000$ p.a.
How much is this per fortnight?

A salon manager is paid $\$1\,145$ per week.
Find her annual salary, using $1$ year $=52$ weeks.

A factory worker is paid $\$1.85$ for each lampshade she assembles.
Find her pay for assembling $240$ lampshades.

A musician is paid a royalty of $6\%$ of the sales of her album.
Find her royalty when the album sales total $\$85\,000$.

A plumber is paid $\$38.50$ per hour and works $8$ hours a day for $5$ days.
He is also paid a confined-space allowance of $\$16$ for each day spent under a house, which was $3$ of the days.
Find his total pay for the week.

A café supervisor earns $\$920$ per week.
Find her leave loading, which is $17.5\%$ of $4$ weeks' pay.

development.question_text:
A baker is paid $\$25.60$ per hour.
In one week he works $38$ ordinary hours, $4$ hours at time and a half and $2$ hours at double time.
Find his total pay for the week.

A warehouse picker is paid $\$27.30$ per hour for the first $38$ hours each week, and time and a half for any hours beyond that.
Find his total pay in a week in which he works $45$ hours.

An electrician is paid $\$34.20$ per hour.
In one week she works $36$ ordinary hours, $6$ hours at time and a half and $2$ hours at double time.
Use equivalent normal hours to find her total pay.

A hotel porter is paid $\$1\,375.40$ per fortnight and works $26$ hours each week.
Find his hourly rate of pay.

A hairdresser is paid $\$4\,368$ per month.
Find her weekly pay.
Convert to a yearly amount first — do not divide by $4$.

A cabinet maker is paid $\$6.40$ for each of the first $40$ drawers he makes, then $\$8.15$ for every drawer after that.
Find his pay for making $62$ drawers.

A courier is paid $\$4.75$ for each parcel delivered.
Find the smallest number of parcels she must deliver to earn at least $\$500$.
development.solution_text:
$\dfrac{\$500}{\$4.75}$
$=105.26\ldots$
Part of a parcel cannot be delivered, so she must deliver $106$ parcels.

development.question_text:
A flooring salesperson is paid a retainer of $\$380$ per week plus a commission of $3.5\%$ of sales.
Find her total pay in a week in which she sells $\$12\,400$ worth of flooring.

A tool salesman earns a commission of $12.5\%$ of all weekly sales in excess of $\$4\,000$.
Find his commission in a week in which his sales are $\$17\,600$.

A kitchen showroom pays its salespeople $4\%$ commission on the first $\$15\,000$ of sales and $6.5\%$ on any sales above $\$15\,000$.
Find the commission earned on sales of $\$38\,000$.

A café cook is paid $\$27.50$ per hour for a $38$-hour week.
At the end of the year his employer pays him a bonus of $5\%$ of his yearly wages.
Find his total pay for the year.

An electrician's assistant earns $\$61\,464$ per year.
He takes $4$ weeks of annual leave and is paid leave loading of $17.5\%$.
Find his total holiday pay.

mastery.question_text:
Marco is a chef paid $\$31.60$ per hour.
In one week he works $38$ ordinary hours, $3$ hours on Saturday at time and a half and $4$ hours on Sunday at double time.
He is also paid a split-shift allowance of $\$18.50$ for each of $2$ split shifts.
Find his total pay for the week, to the nearest cent.

A tiler worked $30$ hours at his normal rate, $4$ hours at time and a half and $3$ hours at double time, and was paid $\$1\,041.60$ altogether.
Find his normal hourly rate.

A salesperson at an appliance store is offered two ways of being paid: $\$540$ per week plus $2.5\%$ of sales, or $5\%$ of sales with no retainer.
Find the weekly sales figure at which the two offers pay exactly the same.
mastery.solution_text:
Let $x$ be the weekly sales.
$540 + 0.025x = 0.05x$
$540 = 0.025x$
$x = \dfrac{540}{0.025}$
$=21\,600$
The offers pay the same on weekly sales of $\$21\,600.00$.

mastery.question_text:
A warehouse worker is paid leave loading of $17.5\%$ of $4$ weeks' pay, and his loading came to $\$850.50$.
Find his normal hourly rate if he works a $36$-hour week.
